questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience what it was like studying in a different country, as I always considered going abroad for my studies. But mostly it was to try something new.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was at an online event for economics students where there was a lot of information about the different destinations. I learned that Pantheon Sorbonne in Paris was a good place to go, no matter what field of economics that interests you. Besides that, I thought it would be fun to live in Paris, even though I have no connection to the place.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It's France.. Everything was a bit messy, but I figured it out along the way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There where some very general introductory meetings. But the people working in the administration were quite responsive, so you could always figure it out, if you were unsure about something.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I can recommend Cite Universitaire. It was pretty easy, you just apply online throught the Fondation Danoise online.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't think you can live on campus in Paris. But living is pretty similar to living "on campus", so if you want that experience, I can recommend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: More difficult to find a place if you want to live in an apartment, I think.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: University of Copenhagen had forgotten to send my nomination, so everything happened a bit last minute, but it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Well the course registration online page crashed, so we had to sign up manually in person instead. But I did end up getting all the courses I wanted, so can't really complain.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In person help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
10/10.
There was a waiting list for some of the courses I wanted, but they signed me up anyways when I showed up in person.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient, do not worry too much, it's very french and you always find a solution (and show up in person and talk to them). Don't stress too much about deadlines, they don't.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did MA courses. The level was fine, a little less math-heavy compared to KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only lectures and no small classes. Less slides. But the style of the teaching depended a lot on the specific course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Political economy, environmental economics, epistemology and history of economic thought, development economics, industrial economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can recommend epistemology and history of economic thought if you want to try a very french way of teaching. Otherwise I really enjoyed development economics, the level is high, the slides are great, and if you like economic history, you will definitely enjoy this.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to spend A LOT of money if you want to have fun in Paris (it is worth it though).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It turned out to be both more and less expensive to go out and eat, since it is a little less expensive than Copenhagen, but you do it way more so..

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not at the institution itself, but made use of sports at the cite universitaire.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Tennis.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of Paris and see the area around. But just have fun and experience as much of Paris as you can.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are more rude, but they are really just being honest instead of pleasing you, which you get used to pretty fast. Not knowing french is not that big of a deal, just do your best.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people after lectures. Become part of all the whatsapp groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation of life, the culture of going out for dinner on a tuesday for no particular reason.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not stress. Enjoy it as much as you can while you're there. Be prepared to spend a lot of money.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Email them or talk to them in person, their online systems are terrible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making a lot of new friends. Trying a different style of teaching and examination.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having enough money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
